title: Scribe new takes a JSON spec file
regret_when: Filling a spec by hand costs more than writing the record by hand.
y_statement: In the context of an agent that must write a decision record before the first implementing edit, facing the choice between many command line flags and one structured file, I decided to take a single JSON spec file, to achieve one reviewable artifact per record, accepting that the agent has to write a temp file first.
question: How does the decide skill hand a full decision record to the CLI?
criteria:
- Every body section can be filled without shell quoting.
- The generated identity fields cannot be supplied by the caller.
constraints:
- The skill can only run scribe through Bash.
- The record must validate before anything is written.

options.option: One JSON spec file passed with --spec
options.for: No shell quoting; the whole record is one reviewable artifact

options.option: One command line flag per field
options.against: Multi-paragraph body sections do not survive shell quoting
options.why_rejected: The body sections are prose, not flags

decision: The CLI reads a JSON spec file named by --spec, generates the identity and lifecycle fields itself, renders the body from the record template, and writes nothing unless the whole record validates.
consequences:
- Positive: the same spec shape works from a skill, a test, or a human.
- Negative: the caller writes a temp file first.
- Measure: records rejected by the validator before writing.
evidence_pointers: docs/build/03-plan-v2.md section 4.9, the scribe new paragraph
